title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics of 'ateliers'. An atelier is a set M of 'figures' (closed cells) X, each with a boundary ∂X. It is a combinatorial-tame substitute for polyhedral or regular CW structures, in line with the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse.

Notation:
- A complex F has a face poset F̃ of figures.
- F' ≼ F means F' is a subdivision of F.
- A subdivision comes with a carrier map φ: F̃' → F̃, sending each cell of F' to the smallest cell of F containing it.
- G ≤ F means G is a subcomplex; G̃ ⊂ F̃ is a closed (downward-closed) subset, as the marginal 'sous ens. fermé' indicates.

Th 14 (previous page): if G ≤ F and G' ≼ G, some subdivision F' of F induces G'. The proof is meant to reduce, via gluing of subdivisions, to the case F = X a single figure.

The Remarque asks for a canonical, least fine (maximal for ≼) such F'. This page states it as the optional axiom At (fac) 14 bis: F' can be chosen so that only G is subdivided. Concretely:
- The square G̃' ↪ F̃' over G̃ ↪ F̃ (vertical maps φ) is cartesian, i.e. G̃' = φ⁻¹(G̃).
- φ restricts to an order isomorphism F̃' \ G̃' ≅ F̃ \ G̃.
- For ξ ∈ G̃' and η ∈ F̃' outside G̃', we have ξ ≤ η iff φ(ξ) ≤ φ(η).
- Hence F̃' = G̃' ⊔ (F̃ \ G̃), with the mixed order pulled back along φ, determined up to unique isomorphism.

Cells not in G survive as single cells whose boundaries are now subdivided. Grothendieck presumes such an F' is unique, namely the largest (least fine) subdivision of F inducing G' on G.

When enough figures are finite, so transfinite induction can be avoided, he expects 14 bis to be equivalent to the local axiom At (fac) 14 ter: for X ∈ M and F' ≼ ∂X there is a unique X' ∈ M with X' ≼ X and ∂X' = F'. In words, a cell with re-subdivided boundary is again a cell, in a unique way. The face poset of X' is that of F' with a new top element.

The next page notes that this fails for simplicial ateliers: a triangle with a subdivided edge is not a simplex. So 14 ter singles out polyhedral/CW-like ateliers as opposed to simplicial ones. The problem served is the existence of canonical minimal extensions of subdivisions from a subcomplex, i.e. relative subdivision theory.
errors: The order condition 'ξ ≤ η ssi φ(ξ) ≤ φ(η)' for ξ ∈ G̃', η ∈ F̃' cannot hold literally when η is also in G̃', since φ is not order-reflecting inside a subdivision. It must be restricted to η ∈ F̃' \ G̃', with the order on G̃' being its own.

The uniqueness of the least fine F' and the equivalence of 14 bis with 14 ter are only conjectured ('je présume'), not proved. The equivalence also needs Th 14's gluing and finiteness hypotheses, which are left vague.

ideas.what: Minimal extension of a subdivision of a closed subcomplex to the whole complex: only cells of G are subdivided, and the face poset is the pullback/pushout along the carrier map (cartesian square).
ideas.modern_name: Relative/extension of subdivisions for polyhedral or regular CW complexes; carrier map of a subdivision
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology (Whitehead, Zeeman, Hudson); face-poset formulation in combinatorial topology (Björner's CW posets, 1984)

ideas.what: Axiom that any subdivision of the boundary of a cell yields a unique cell structure with that boundary (At 14 ter); it distinguishes polyhedral/CW ateliers from simplicial ones.
ideas.modern_name: Closure of cell classes under boundary re-subdivision; regular CW posets, where adding a top element over a sphere poset gives a cell
ideas.usually_credited_to: Björner (CW posets); polyhedral vs simplicial complexes folklore

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'ateliers' as a framework for tame topology / analysis situs.
ideas.modern_name: Close in spirit to o-minimal structures / tame topology, combinatorial cell complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Shiota (o-minimality); Grothendieck's programme in Esquisse d'un programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions topologie modérée, but not ateliers

missed.claim: Conjectured uniqueness of the least fine subdivision extending G', and its equivalence with the local axiom 14 ter, are left unproved. In poset terms this is an easy exercise for CW-poset-like ateliers, but it is part of the unexplored 'atelier' axiomatics.
missed.quote: Je présume qu'on doit pouvoir prouver qu'un tel F' est unique, comme le plus grand des [subdivisions] de F induisant G' sur G
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It would be a lemma in any formalization of Grothendieck's atelier approach to tame topology. The broader atelier framework remains essentially unstudied.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a natural, routine axiom about extending subdivisions minimally, essentially known in PL/CW combinatorics. Its interest lies only in being part of the little-known, unpublished 'ateliers' axiomatization of tame topology.
transcription_corrections: The heading label is 'At (fac) 14 bis' (atelier axiom, facultative), not 'Ax'. Likewise 'At (fac) 14 ter' at the bottom.
'plus grand des sous-ensembles[?] de F' should most likely read 'plus grand des subdivisions de F'.
'sous ens. fermé' is a note under the bottom arrow G̃ ↪ F̃, meaning G̃ is a closed subset.
φ* in the order condition is just φ (the carrier map). The subscript on G̃' is likely spurious or a stray mark.
Marginal note near 'figures finies' is unclear; the 'unicité ou multiplicité' reading is doubtful.
